sentences.text:
Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the Petition Papers, this Court declines indulgence in the matter for the following reasons:
(a) The first submission of learned Sr. Counsel Mr. Naragund appearing for the Petitioners that the acquisition has lapsed under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act is principally based upon the judgment of a Coordinate Bench of this Court in W.P.No.50185/2014 filed by the vendors of the Housing Society against the State &
KHB.
The Housing Society as such was not a party to the same.
The writ petition was disposed off on 03.08.2015 declaring "...The land acquisition in respect of the petition schedule property is deemed to have lapsed under the 'New Land Acquisition Act".

However, this judgment was put in challenge by the KHB in W.A.Nos. 2632 - 2633/2015 (LA- KHB) and it was modified to the effect that the acquisition was left intact and the vendors of the Housing Society i.e., land owners would accept the compensation.

Paragraph No.4 of the judgment dated 29.10.2015 made in Writ Appeal reads as under:
"We record, further, that the authorities have agreed to pay Rs.12,46,56,000/-
(Rupees twelve crore forty six lakh fifty six thousand) only as compensation for 49 guntas of land and Rs.2,79,84,000/- (Rupees two crore seventy nine lakh eighty four thousand) only for 11 guntas of land."
In view of the above, the Petitioners cannot claim that the acquisition of the land in question has lapsed.

(b) Learned Sr. Advocate Mr. Dhyan Chinnappa appearing for the Housing Board is more than justified in contending that the acquisition having been duly accomplished long before the 2013 Act came into force, challenge to the same at this length of time cannot be maintained.

This acquisition commenced with the issuance of Preliminary Notification on 23.06.1990; it was followed by the Final Notification dated 30.05.1992; the Award was made on 23.06.1993; possession of the land was taken on 20.12.1999 and lastly Section 16(2) Notification was gazetted on 07.02.2000.
There is absolutely no explanation offered for the enormous delay & latches brooked in the matter.
It hardly needs to be sated that belated challenge to the acquisition is not favoured by the Courts, the consequences of voiding of acquisition being undesirable.

Added, the challenge to the acquisition by the Housing Society in W.P.No.29940/1992 was dismissed on 06.08.1998 on the ground of delay &
latches; similarly, original land owners' W.P.No.28022-28955/2011 calling the acquisition in question was negatived on 28.09.2011.
Even W.A.No.4753-60/2012 was also dismissed on 19.03.2013.

(c) Mr. Dhyan Chinnappa, learned Sr. Advocate is also right in contending that Petitioners being the buyers post acquisition lack locus standii to call in question the subject acquisition vide SHIV KUMAR & ANOTHER Vs. UNION of INDIA & OTHERS, (2019) 10 SCC 229, wherein, at Paragraph No.26 it is observed as under:
S Mahendra Kumar vs State Of Karnataka on 13 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189731703/
4

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: S Mahendra Kumar vs State Of Karnataka

sentences.text: "...No declaration can be sought by a purchaser under Section 24 that acquisition has lapsed, effect of which would be to get back the land.
They cannot seek declaration that acquisition made under the 1894 Act has lapsed by the challenge to the proceedings of taking possession under the 1894 Act.
Such right was not available after the purchase in 2000 and no such right has been provided to the purchasers under the 2013 Act also.
Granting a right to question acquisition would be against the public policy and the law which prohibits such transactions; ..."

Heavy reliance placed by Mr. Naragund on GOVERNMENT (NCT OF DELHI) vs. MANAV DHARAM TRUST, (2017) 6 SCC 715 for the lapsing of acquisition would not yield any milk inasmuch as, the above observations have been made by the Larger Bench of the Apex Court holding this decision to be per incurium.

entities.text: GOVERNMENT (NCT OF DELHI) vs. MANAV DHARAM TRUST, (2017) 6 SCC 715
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At Paragraph No. 28, it has been observed "We hold that Division Bench in Manav Dharam Trust does not lay down the law correctly.
Given the several binding precedents which are available and the provisions of the 2013 Act, we cannot follow the decision in Manav Dharam Trust and overrule it..."

(d) The submission of Mr. Naragund that vendors of the Housing Society having played fraud had secured certain judgments (in W.P. No. 50185/2014, disposed off on 03.08.2012 &
W.A.Nos.2632-263/2015, disposed off on 29.10.2015) and on that basis, they have received the compensation and therefore, his clients being the innocent buyers from the Housing Society are entitled to be paid the said amount, of course, in proportion to their sale prices, does not merit a deeper examination at the hands of this Court.
True it is that Lord Edward Coke centuries ago roared that fraud vitiates everything.

The Apex Court resounded the same in S. P.
CHANGAVALARIYA NAIDU vs. JAGANNATH AIR 1994 SC 853.

S. P.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Firstly, the said land owners are not parties eo nominee to this Petition; secondly, there is no privity of contract between the Petitioners on the one hand and the said land owners, on the other, since they have bought the property from the Cooperative Housing Society.
In the absence of such a privity, this Court is not sure if the doctrine of feeding the grant by estoppel can be readily invoked.
Lastly, the - 10 - Housing Society having lost the land in acquisition could not have conveyed title to the Petitioners vide nemo dat quad non habet, also cannot be ignored.

(e) Learned Sr. Advocate, Mr. Dhyan Chinnappa appearing for the Housing Board submits that, in respect of alleged fraudulent payment of compensation in crores of rupees, a disciplinary inquiry has been going on.
It hardly needs to be stated that such an inquiry cannot be kept pending ad infinitum.
If fraud, fabrication & duplicity are established in the inquiry, a cause of action may accrue even on that basis in favour of the petitioners or such other aggrieved persons.

Therefore,
there is an eminent need for the expeditious accomplishment of the said inquiry and the penal/remedial action taken, if any.

The Government also should supervise the on-going inquiry,
and the Auditor General of the State should also look into the matter in view of enormity of the payment of public money by way of compensation.

sentences.text: (f) All the above having been said, Petitioners should be reserved liberty to frame a proper suit, at least for - 11 - getting the compensation/damages from the Housing Society or the vendors of the Housing Society who have allegedly defrauded them, and this Court.
All contentions in this regard need to be kept open, the observations hereinabove made being confined to the disposal of Writ Petition not foreclosing any of them.
In the above circumstances and with the above observations, this Writ Petition is disposed off.
Liberty is reserved to the Petitioners to tap the suit remedy in accordance with law.
If such a suit is filed, the same shall be tried & disposed off within an outer limit of one year.

Registry to send a copy of this judgment to the Accountant General, Karnataka, by speed post immediately.
Costs made easy.
